categories.name: Overall aesthetic
categories.summary: A dark, archival internet-horror documentary. Most of the running time is web pages, comments and photos laid out as tilted 3D sheets on a dark ground, cut against long stretches of raw source footage. Graphics are desaturated and grainy; raw footage keeps its own colour and age. In the 5 references, motion graphics make up 45-80% of the clips.

rules.text: Grade to measured targets pooled over every used range, never one frame; a landed grade is never carried to another case as a preset.
Night footage gets a smaller lift; one global grade turns night into grey haze; lift per range, not per case or series.
Leave saturation high enough that a mono echo keeps its meaning.
Measure every placed frame's mean luma; swap a near-black shot rather than rescuing it in the grade.
Fill and grade only as much as asked; propose the rest rather than doing it.
Measure darkness inside the picture area on vertical or pillarboxed footage, not the full frame.
Night footage is lifted until it reads; look is muted colour with reds kept, deep contrast, soft bloom, vignette and grain.
Never stack creative LUTs: at most one LUT per shot, blended by intensity; a missing LUT stops the plan and is never substituted.
Warrior Mind LUT pick by pooled brightness: above 65 daylight, 28-65 main night warm, below 28 dark-footage lift; the near-black evidence LUT is chosen by hand only.
A shot with mean luma under about 8 (8-bit) counts as near-black and is swapped, not graded.
Fix dark night raw by lifting (exposure +1.9, shadows +45, blacks +5, contrast +10); blacks -10 crushes it and blacks +20 turns grey.
Treat measured look figures as targets, not directions, and pool every used source range before grading because one frame can invert the answer.
Grade after the cut is locked, in order exposure, white balance, contrast, saturation, creative look; match shots before making any look good.
Use a blurred enlarged fill behind a pillarboxed or letterboxed clip, with a frame-count guard.

categories.name: Editing rhythm
categories.summary: A block is a run of shots with one look (for example, all tilted-page shots), ending when the look changes. Expect 4-6 blocks per minute. Graphic blocks run 8-11 s; raw-footage blocks run 11-16 s and up to 27 s; title cards 2-4 s. Inside a block the picture keeps changing, so the cut still feels quick (the 60 s sample averaged 1.4 s per shot).

rules.text: Hold graphic blocks 8-11 s and raw-footage blocks 11-16 s; let a raw moment run to 25 s or more when it is the evidence.
Keep title and date cards to 2-4 s.

evidence.label: v01 · Gold year title '1996' over blur

rules.text: Change the picture inside a block (a new page, photo or push) every 1-3 s while narration runs.

evidence.label: v01 · Still photos: Brandes portrait, bathroom, cough syrup

rules.text: Never run narration over empty black: if the ground is black, something sits on it (text, a page, a photo).

rules.text: Read the narration, then look at the footage, before choosing any shot.
One scene, one clip: length is not the rule, one image per clip is; do not cut a continuous scene into many same-picture cuts.
Dense, eventful narration wants tight cuts; long exposition with nothing to show gets fewer, longer holds, never cuts for no informational reason.
Cut on the clause (midpoint of the pause), not by feel, and never shorter than about 2 s; shot length is an output of the narration.
When a proper noun sits inside a clause, the picture arrives exactly on that noun.
The picture must be the literal subject of its clause (right time of day, right register), one picture per list item.
Search for the action the narration describes, not its noun; if a line cannot be shown, cover the destination, never a stand-in actor.
A different time range of the same scene is not a different picture; vary the framing.
Check head, middle and tail of a picked range; a pick that works at 4 s can straddle a cut at 8 s.
Dark is not black: a dark but readable range can be the best material; lift it to judge it before discarding.
A freeze is a choice, not a mechanism: repeat the moving footage instead of freezing, freeze only for an examination beat the narration names.
A reveal mark (ring/box) needs a still camera; choose the calmest window.
Fill from the case's own source between neighbouring evidence beats; stock last; raw footage 70%+ under narration.
Derive the fill strategy from what the source is; a single-framing source is monotonous, so do not manufacture cuts to hide it.
A still image inside a footage video stays short (a scanned clipping capped at 16 s).
Slow a shot to hold the clause's state rather than cut to the wrong picture.
A short source forces reuse: spread the windows, play repeats as motion, make the last raw the longest.
Never shave a shot or leave a 1-frame black gap; overlap instead.
Pacing has a shape per section (open wide, tighten in the middle, open up for the payoff); held shots (2x median) are 57-72% of runtime.
A repeated device in one case changes grammar the second time (plate, then card over footage), never the same shot twice in 20 s.
A burned-in instrument readout (thermal, CCTV, bodycam stamp) is allowed when it is the clause's subject; the camera's own flaws stay as proof.
Phone-vertical clips get a blurred fill behind; old 4:3 archival keeps clean black bars.
Check each source for creator cards, captions, end cards, re-uploader overlays and watermarks before picking ranges; re-scan after any extension.
A crop that leaves a fragment of creator text is worse than none; anchor it so none shows.
After any hand edit by the owner, re-derive the clause map from real positions; the owner's own placements also get checked.
Check every raw out-edge against the word it ends on so a cut never lands inside a word.
The last line of a paragraph that teases the next beat gets one or two teaser shots of that moment.
Never cut mid-speech in a raw; raw clips start and end on word edges (use word timings).
Never cross the source creator's own edit, and leave no stray 1-10 frame fragments of another shot (including raw tails).
Evidence beats: hold uncut, slow the replay, push in slowly; arrows or circles only when the target is certain (track it if it moves).
Jump-cut dead air inside a raw clip; extend raws at word boundaries to hit the target runtime.
Pack the case start: before the first raw, layer 5-8 real details (source page, date, channel, location, document or photo, teasers).
Preview stills of every new device against the reference still before rendering; fix size, position and timing.
When the user reports a problem at a timestamp, find the exact cause and fix it everywhere, not only there.
Narration cut points keep at least 120 ms lead and about 400 ms tail before a raw.

rules.text: Never play a source range containing an internal cut; when the source runs out use another angle of the same scene.
Every animation fully enters then holds readable: at least 1.5 s plus 0.3 s per word, total at least 3 s (pages 4-8 s, maps 3-5 s, name tag 2.1-2.9 s); entries 10+ frames.
Device repetition limits: series devices repeat every case; page treatments 3-4 uses each; everything else at most about 5 per video and never in consecutive cases.

rules.text: When a repetitive device is removed, refill the spot with a new situation-fitting device if the narration explains, names, counts, dates, locates or compares something the footage does not show.
A designed plate never opens empty or sits still: first element lands within about 8 frames of the cut, sparse graphics drift at a visible rate.
Replays are real-time (no half-speed or frame doubling), with a crop or angle change, entered 0.2 s after the last word.
Cut B-roll only at a sentence end or when the narration changes topic, on the pause midpoint or the word boundary, never by feel or on a round number.
Change the picture on the spoken noun: each clause gets the literal picture of what it names, and the picture must not run a shot ahead of the voice.
One continuous scene is one clip: do not chop it into short cuts, and fill a removed cut by extending the neighbouring clip.
Pull the raw clip's head back so its picture runs ahead of its own audio when the narration is only describing what the raw clip is about to show.
Do not fill narration gaps with frozen frames; replay the source as motion (a frozen talking face reads as a broadcast fault).
In vlog footage the face dominates, so the non-face seconds are the fill budget; raw footage may run out and leave unavoidable black.
Generic pacing: B-roll under narration changes every 2-4 s, nothing static past about 7 s without a reason, cut on motion, and about 90% of cuts are hard cuts.
Hold a B-roll beat for the time needed to read the picture; a plate or highlight runs 3-4 s, max 5 s, and a longer beat is split into two clips at different camera angles.

categories.name: Transitions
categories.summary: Most edits are straight cuts (31 of 34 in the 60 s sample); a straight cut is not a transition. Each transition has one job (rules 3 and 9): VHS for a chapter change, dip to black for a new date, place or time period, crossfade inside a montage, glitch when something breaks. VHS transition is one group of 15 variants, each with its built-in SFX. Crossfade and dip to black have no SFX.

rules.text: Cut straight unless one of the jobs below applies.
Mark a chapter or case change with a dip to black into the title card. Use a VHS transition only rarely (an article or a page).

evidence.label: v03 · VHS rewind to blue screen

rules.title: VHS transition
rules.text:
One group. When a rule says VHS, pick any one below (or the tape start / rewind from the references). Each plays its built-in SFX: keep it, change only the level. Never use Color Bars or Shaky Flashy (too loud).
  - Color Channel Offset: low hum that swells into a distorted warble, then fades (turn down 4 dB)
  - Static & Skew: steady crackling static with a buzz under it, flat level
  - Warp & Flicker: two soft ticks, then a low warble that builds
  - Flicker With Static: a steady buzz chopped on and off with the flicker
  - Warp Bars: bright hiss that swells at the end
  - Quick Flicker: short low thump (bass blip) (turn down 3 dB)
  - Quick Static: short static zap
  - Seeing Double: steady high tape whine (about 2 kHz)
  - Skipping Warp: a buzz that stutters 2-3 times as the frame skips
  - Warp Tracking: flat tracking hiss that jumps up at the end
  - Color Bleed: short bright white-noise hiss
  - Stretch Warp: hiss and whine that rise from quiet to loud (limit the click at the end)
  - Static Woosh: low rumbling woosh that builds (turn down 4 dB)
  - Wavy Burst 1: short buzzy burst (the same sound as Wavy Burst 2) (turn down 3 dB)
  - Wavy Burst 2: short buzzy burst (the same sound as Wavy Burst 1) (turn down 3 dB)
Use a short glitch (1-4 s) when a broadcast cuts out or the story jumps.

rules.text: Dip only at section handovers, about one per 50 s, not at every raw boundary.
Dissolve the exits from evidence, hard-cut the entries into evidence so the riser lands; a clip under about 2.7 s takes one transition only.
Dissolve and dip width is about 1.2 s (owner approved); never 2.0 s.
A hard cut on the hook (cold open into first raw) is fine and needs no transition.
Transitions never cross the creator's own cut; a plate needs material (handles) on both sides, about 0.6 s.
Never judge a transition at its cut frame; sample inside it.
Dissolve the exits out of raw evidence and hard-cut the entries into it, so the riser and impact land on the cut.
The boundary between a B-roll montage and a raw clip is a dip to black of about 1-1.5 s, not a cross dissolve; dissolves stay inside the montage.
Transition coverage percentage is an output of the policy, never a target to hit.
Transition lengths that read right at 30 fps: whip 4-8 frames, dissolve 10-20, slow dissolve 30-45, fade to black 30-60; a transition that draws attention must be deliberate.

A bright white flash that blooms into a reveal: an evidence page, a photo or a shock line. Full white for up to 10 frames, then it fades into the picture. Only into reveals, a few per video. SFX: a camera-flash pop or a low impact hit.

categories.summary: All added text is VCR OSD Mono (rule 2). The references use text sparingly: one-word chapter titles, years and dates, file-name labels and names, each centred and held for 2-4 s, plus on-screen typing into search boxes.

rules.text: Set every added title, date, label and caption in VCR OSD Mono (rule 2).
Chapter titles are one or two words in capitals, centred over blurred, darkened footage.
Label names, years and titles in gold; file names and translations of foreign text in white.

rules.text: Show searches by typing them into the real search box, letter by letter.
Draw and look at the highlight rectangle on the source before rendering; quote the comment in full and let the highlight pick the claim.
Highlight blend follows the page: screen on dark, multiply on light; red on dark, yellow on light.
Spell proper nouns from the source's title or description, never from the transcript; list place names for caption casing.
A title matches the shot under it and lands on the word that names the place.
A title on a bright plate needs a scrim; move it off a chyron.
Text safe area: 80 px from the sides, 100 px top/bottom at 1080p; headline at least 84 px, supporting at least 44 px.
Titles and overlays fade in and out, never pop; raw subtitles and small notes cut hard on and off.
Delete caption fragments and captions that overhang the raw ("And.", half sentences).

Each case opens on the project's case title card (PROJECT/graphics/hyperframes/out/camping8/v3/card4-cN.mp4): the case's own footage, darkened with a vignette, a small gold VCR 'CASE N' over a big white condensed title, 4.5 s. Dip to black into it and out of it.
Never show a creator's description when it holds personal or payment data.
Captions are for creator speech only, never the narration; hand-fix every transcription error; bleep profanity with a dash in the caption.
A label's form follows its meaning (place = map or HUD callout, date = data row, person = anchored tag, number = one still big number, never a counter); never the same lower-third twice in a row.
Text is always native editor text; never a static title card, the title is a wall of tiles that flip to clips on the words.
Speaker-anchored captions on raws; name tag shown the first time a key person speaks or is named.
Put the place name on every wide or aerial establishing shot, large with the region small beneath, in VCR OSD Mono.
Keep titles at least 80 px from the sides (title safe about 90%); one idea per card.
Captions are for raw clip speech only, never the narration. Each caption sits in a solid black box: no drop shadow, no outline. Make it with Premiere's Text tool, in VCR OSD Mono.

categories.name: Music and sound
categories.summary: Narration leads. Loudness is measured in LUFS (the average loudness of the whole mix on a loudness meter): the references sit at -17.6 to -14.4 LUFS, 4 of the 5 near -17. The voice is calm, 155-195 words per minute, with 4-8 pauses of 0.6 s or more per minute (median 0.8 s). Music is a low bed (8.4 dB under the voice in the 60 s sample). Raw clips bring their own sound, faded by rule 8.

rules.text: Master to -17 LUFS integrated; keep the voice clear and steady.
Keep music 8 dB under the narration on the loudness meter, as a dark ambient bed, not a melody.
Let the raw footage's own sound play when it is the evidence, with the narration silent.

evidence.label: v05 · Witch video ending, source audio
v05 · Abdullah footage: doors and noises

rules.text: Leave a pause of 0.8 s after a disturbing line before the next sentence.
Fade raw clip audio by rule 8.

rules.title: VHS transition SFX
rules.text: Every VHS transition plays the SFX built into it (static, hiss, buzz, warble or whine; see Transitions). Keep that SFX; only change its level. Keep it short, under the narration, and near the set median of -23.6 dB RMS. No VHS SFX may stand out as loud noise.
No creator audio under narration: B-roll over voice-over is picture only.
When the beat is the raw clip, pre-lap its picture; do not cut away to the same scene; gaps under about 5 s are a head extension.
Two raws after one prose block: the second gets no pre-roll.
Choose each raw on what is said in it: the soundbite that corroborates the paragraph; quoted dialogue beats a timestamp hint.
A raw after every paragraph (minimum 8 s), and a video never ends on narration over black.
Let narration breathe: cut where the waveform rests, keep narrator pauses (comma 0.2 s, sentence 0.35 s, paragraph 0.5 s); never tighten more than about 15%.
Narration is only 56-72% of runtime; leave footage audio and silence, long speech gaps are the style, do not fill them.
Verify every narration take by transcript against the script before building.
A verdict, a prayer or a plea is never scored: pick the silent beat from the content.
A source peaking at 0 dB cannot be brought up with gain; measure mean and peak and let the owner choose.
A raw picture keeps running about 1.25 s under the next narration with its audio ducked to -24 dB, and the creator's voice is never audible under narration.
Tighten AI narration gaps: sentence ends 0.25-0.35 s, commas 0.15-0.20 s.
Remove the source creators' background music but keep ambience and scares.
Voice-over and clip speech never overlap; the music bed ducks but is never dead (never below -50 dB for 1.2 s).
Music bed about -31 LUFS, 3-7 cues per case crossfaded 6 s; a chapter card is never digital silence.
Score the audio starts (the J-cut entry) precisely, never randomly: risers end on the evidence entry, impacts start on it.
Never add music or SFX unless asked; when asked, build it fully with sane static levels and no ducking.
Never put music over a silent "raw"; use 1-2 bed sections from different parts of a track and never the same (track, start) twice; adjacent cases never open on the same track.
rules.origin: review-2026-11-09 LC-83 | OT s2; CS s12

rules.text: House SFX levels: impact -8, sub -5, riser -10, suck -14, vhs -18, texture -24 dB; hottest element about -8.5 dB peak.
SFX are atmosphere, not punctuation: cluster them before a new section instead of punching every cut.
Vary the scare: no two hand-offs get the same treatment; save the biggest hit for the act break and finale.
Mark the exits too: the return from evidence to narration gets its own low air-suck sound.
Layer sound: a sub only on the biggest beats, a seamless room tone, one register sound naming the medium (tape click, radio static).
Never drop a diegetic sound effect blind; look at the frames first.
No SFX file repeats inside a series; reviewers hear the reuse.
A texture SFX is earned only when the narration names the sound.
SFX stay restrained and tied to transitions (impacts on flashes, whooshes on slides, glitch hits).
SFX sit 6-8 dB under the voice-over; never invent SFX; rotate variants; look-here marks are silent.
rules.origin: review-2026-11-09 LC-93 | GX; CS s7, s11

rules.text: Level SFX to the raw voice-over; an SFX set 15-20 dB too loud is a rejected mix.
rules.origin: review-2026-11-09 LC-94 | CS s11; OT s5

rules.text: Clips placed over narration are picture only: strip their audio (ffmpeg -an or delete the clips); muting the track is not enough.
Match the level so narration and raw audio sit at 0 to -6 dB on the meter; bake the gain into the file and do not use clip gain or faders.
Put room tone under everything so silence never sounds like a dropout; digital-silent chapter cards were heard as an audio jump cut and now get a bed under each.
Verify every narration take by transcribing the whole file and diffing it against the script; a wrong take can share its opening words.
Narration is pre-stripped of silence by the owner; skip any automatic silence-cut phase.
The voice is chosen per video; ask which voice, never assume the last one.
Use one music track per video, extended to length by cross-fading the track into itself, never two stitched tracks.
Keep music bass-heavy and dark: roughly 25 cues per video, centroid near 260 Hz, bed near -17.7 dBFS.
Score the hand-off between a narration passage and an evidence block with a riser ending on the evidence entry and an impact starting on it; read the audio starts, not the video cuts.
Place risers where the script says 'watch closely' or 'listen', not randomly.
Vary the beats and escalate the impacts; a formulaic repeat was rejected, and the biggest impact goes on the act break and the final block.
Leave one hand-off per case unscored, chosen from what the block says (a legal verdict, a prayer, a plea, a line where silence is the answer).
Every SFX clip is a different file (127 unique), each baked to its own level.

categories.name: Storytelling
categories.summary: An investigation told in order of discovery: a cold open on the most disturbing material, the narration posing the question over raw clips, then the evidence trail (searches, archived pages, comments, broadcasts) one step at a time, chapter titles at each turn, and a narrated sign-off with credits. No host on camera: the whole video is narration over raw clips.

rules.text: Open cold on the most disturbing footage, broken up with glitch tears, before any introduction; then let the narration pose the question over raw clips.

evidence.label: v05 · Cold open: jinn footage, glitch tears

rules.text: Follow the evidence in the order it was found: search, archived page, post, comment, footage.

evidence.label: v01 · Wayback calendar for discord.com, push to 1996
v01 · r/scottandtomoko post with news link

rules.text: Name each chapter with a short title card.
Close the video on the thesis image, held as live footage not a freeze.
End on the next case's picture when the narration turns to it (teaser).
Verify the narration against footage before planning picture; search the case before illustrating it; use a different true document if the true one contradicts the beat.
Open each case with a dense, layered opener; the intro is a teaser montage with every cut on a narration word.
Send the first one or two cases for approval before doing the rest.
Case title card: use the project's card design (card4-cN.mp4), case footage darkened under a small gold VCR 'CASE N' and a big white condensed title, 4.5 s, with a dip to black before and after it.
rules.origin: review-2026-11-09 LC-167 | EK editing_rules/CASE_STRUCTURE.md; ER r.134

rules.text: Build the picture to the script: if narration names a place or document you cannot source, change the beat instead of showing a lookalike, since an uncaptioned stand-in still reads as the named thing.
Cover the destination the narration names, never the walker, so the picture survives a re-record.
Never fabricate a document about a real place or institution; say nothing on screen about a staged origin when the owner decides so.
Run the reference analysis first and never edit from a text description of a reference.

rulebook.text: Mood is horror, always. Every picture, text, movement and sound adds dread or unease. Nothing bright, cute or playful unless it is glitched, desaturated or distorted so it feels wrong. One exception: the white flash transition (rule 3).

All text you add uses the VCR OSD Mono font: dates, labels, captions, comment cards. No second font. One exception: the case title card copies the project's card design (small gold VCR 'CASE N' over a big white condensed title). Captured pages, posts and broadcasts keep their own fonts.

Between shots, cut straight or use one of these transitions: crossfade, dip to black, VHS (any approved variant from the VHS set, with its SFX), glitch, white flash or split-screen wipe. Most transitions are crossfades (about 1.2 s) and dips to black. Use VHS and the white flash (flashbang) only rarely, for example to show an article or page. No other wipes, slides, spins, zoom transitions or shape reveals. One device exception: WarpCard enters on its own warp slide-in.
Shot size is mostly medium. Use close-up or extreme close-up only to point at a detail (a face, a word, a figure in the frame).

Compose to the centre: the subject, title or key line sits on the centre of the frame. Exception: camcorder OSD and CCTV HUD text sits in the corners, because it is part of the device look; the subject still sits centre. The camcorder clock may tick its seconds.

High contrast, dark grade, vintage texture. Treated shots sit at a median brightness of 70-90 on a 0-255 scale. Before the first edit, pick 3-5 texture types for the video (film grain, VHS noise and tracking lines, CRT scanlines and curvature, dust and scratches, light leak), list them in the edit notes, and put at least one on every treated shot.
Every graphic shot moves: pan, zoom or push, tracking, 3D tilt, or wide angle, sometimes with lens distortion. No still graphics.

Raw clip audio: start the audio 1.0 s before its picture cut (pre-roll; less if the source has no 1.0 s of head) and end it with the picture. Fade in over the first 3.22 s and out over the last 2.74 s. If the audio clip is shorter than 5.96 s, multiply both fade lengths by (clip length / 5.96) x 0.98.

Crossfade inside a montage and between most shots. Dip to black between sections (a new date, place or time period). A dip to black is a must at the end of a case, into its title card, and again at the end of the title card. VHS and the white flash are rare: an article, a page, or a rare shock reveal.
No real person on camera as host or presenter. Every video is narration over raw clips; chapter turns use title cards and the narration, never a cut back to a host.
rulebook.title: Narration and raw clips only

rulebook.text: Follow the cut sheet. For each narration beat, its VISUAL, SOURCE and EDIT NOTES decide the picture and the moment each comment or graphic comes in. Do not add a graphic that the cut sheet or the spoken words do not ask for.
rulebook.title: Follow the cut sheet

rulebook.text: Real footage first. Graphics support the footage; they never fill the time. Put comment cards over real footage from the case (as the PROJECT edit does), not on plain black. Show one comment, then go back to the video. Most of the running time is real footage.
rulebook.title: Real footage first

rulebook.text: Show comments as real screenshots of the real YouTube comments when you can. Crop to the comment that matters (do not show the whole section) and highlight only that main comment. The screenshot floats in: it slides up from the bottom of the frame with easing, or it comes in with a slow 3D pan, or a CRT scan reveal (top-to-bottom wipe with a bright scan line, about 1.1 s, at most twice per video); vary them. If the real comment cannot be found, make your own comment card. When a reply follows its parent, the card grows to fit (shape morph) with easing and the reply crossfades in. No hard cut inside one thread.
rulebook.title: Comments on the real page

rulebook.text: Every animation flows: eased in and out (for example ease-in-out cubic), with no snap, no jump and no cut in the middle. Every card enters and exits with an eased fade and scale; it never vanishes in one frame. If an animation is jerky, fix its easing; do not remove it. Every card stays fully on screen and centred, with a safe margin, on every frame.
rulebook.title: Smooth easing, nothing pops

rulebook.text: No still shots. Every shot longer than about 2 s moves: a slow push (2-5 %/s) or a slow drift. This includes raw footage and photos (add motion only; raw footage keeps its own colour).
rulebook.title: No still shots

rulebook.text: When the narration names an animal, object or thing the viewer may not know (for example a raccoon or a tanuki), show a real photo of it with a slow push. Use a free-licence photo (for example Wikimedia Commons) and keep its source and licence in the edit notes.
rulebook.title: Show the thing named

rulebook.text: Raw captions match the raw audio. Each caption starts within 2 frames of its spoken line and ends when the line ends (hold it a little longer only to reach the minimum). The text says what is said. Each caption stays on screen at least 5/6 s and at most 7 s; a line too short for 5/6 s is joined with the next line. Never hold a caption over silence. Exception: a caption that translates text shown on screen stays while that text shows. Check every caption against the audio.
rulebook.title: Captions match the audio

rulebook.text: Feedback loop: every note from the owner becomes a rule in this guide the same day, with a Learnings entry. Before each edit, read the rule book. After each render, check the render against every rule-book line, fix what fails, then deliver.
rulebook.title: Feedback loop

rulebook.text: No ultra-short shots. A narration shot (B-roll, photo or graphic under the narration) is on screen alone, outside its transitions, for at least 3 s. Raw clips keep the length the cut sheet gives. If a beat is too short, extend a neighbouring shot or merge the beat; never squeeze in a quick extra shot.
rulebook.title: No ultra-short shots

rulebook.text: Clean crossfades: during a crossfade or dip, both clips play continuous footage. No source cut (a change of camera shot inside the source) may fall inside the transition or its handles, not even a soft cut between similar shots. A dip to black is an even eased curve: the old clip fades down smoothly over half the dip, the new clip fades up over the other half (never a fast drop to black in a few frames). Overlays (stamps, captions) on a shot appear and go only while the shot plays alone, never during its fades. After each render, check every transition frame by frame in the final file: no frame-difference spike inside a fade.
rulebook.title: Clean crossfades

rulebook.text: When a comment (card or page screenshot) or a title card is on screen, the footage behind it keeps playing, blurred and darkened, so the comment or title is the sharpest and brightest thing in the frame.
rulebook.title: Blur behind comments and title cards

rulebook.text: Nothing sits still for too long. A non-raw shot where nothing happens is changed within about 4-5 s (new footage, new angle or a comment). Long held shots are allowed only for raw clips the cut sheet asks for.
rulebook.title: Nothing still for too long

rulebook.text: A comment stays on screen long enough to read it: at least 3.5 s in total, entry and exit included, and the full time the narration talks about it. Aim for reading time: characters / 15 + 1 s (the narration reading it aloud may cover the rest). If the narration does not give a comment 3.5 s, leave the comment out; never flash a comment in and out. A comment's slide, pan, lift or grow motion never runs during a crossfade or dip of the footage behind it (the comment may stay still on screen across a fade).
rulebook.title: Comments stay long enough to read

rulebook.text: Before every render, run the rule check on the edit list (scratchpad kit: rulecheck.py <edl>). It must pass with no FAIL: narration shots 3 s alone, shots 2.5 s total, captions 5/6-7 s, comments 3.5 s, no overlay motion inside a fade. Before picking a source in-point, scan the source for camera cuts (srcscan.py) so no cut falls in a fade. After render, check every fade in the final file (fadescan.py).
rulebook.title: Rule check before render

rulebook.text: A motion graphic (comment, card) and the blurred footage behind it are one shot. The short-shot rules count it that way: plain footage between two overlays, or between an overlay and a shot change, is either 0 s or at least 3 s alone. Two comments in a row: the next one slides up while the old one leaves, and the blur stays on (no sharp footage flashes between them). A comment that is still on screen when its footage crossfades to a new shot fades out with that shot during the crossfade (opacity follows the fade, no lift); it never leaves just before the fade. Same at entry: a comment can fade in with its shot. A reply thread shows the full thread (parent + reply) from its first frame, with the reply's translation already under it; no grow/morph step, because viewers do not need to read the parent alone.
rulebook.title: Overlay and its footage are one shot

rulebook.text: Easing palette. Default: ease-in-out cubic (power2.inOut), about 1.0 s, for most moves. Cards, labels and titles that land: ease-out quart (power3.out), about 1.1 s. One big reveal per section: ease-out expo (expo.out), about 1.5 s. Slow drifts, pans and glints: ease-in-out sine (sine.inOut), about 1.5 s or longer. Never bounce, elastic or back easing.
rulebook.from: Motion Lab (docs/motion-lab), approved by the owner 2026-11-10
rulebook.title: Easing palette

rulebook.text: The 34 Motion Lab moves approved on 2026-11-10 are in Motion graphics (source user). Vary them: do not use the same comment, title or label move twice in a row. New approved devices: CRT scan reveal for comments, colour-split title settle, camcorder OSD and CCTV HUD corner text, redaction reveal, case dossier, archive terminal, VHS tape label, Please stand by card and 2.5D parallax collage.
rulebook.from: Motion Lab (docs/motion-lab), approved by the owner 2026-11-10
rulebook.title: Approved Motion Lab moves

rulebook.text: Motion graphics are built from real material: footage stills, page screenshots, real-looking players, comments, documents and maps. Do not add film grain, scratches or VHS texture to a graphic. That texture goes once, on the video track, over everything.
rulebook.title: Graphics look real

learnings.note: Just only one thing. Our video won't be using. Any. Real human clips. It will be all narration and row clips only. So there is no need to learn. About how to bring back the camera to the host, it'll be only narration and raw clips.
learnings.text: Our videos have no host on camera: narration over raw clips only, so the reference's host returns are not copied.

learnings.note: Owner review of the 3-6 min CAMPING-8 sample (2026-11-09): no channel credit on raws; comment cards not tied to the narration; captions must match the raw audio; jerky card cuts, card must grow (morph) smoothly with a crossfade; too many cards, show real footage; follow the cut sheet; too many still shots, add movement; show a real raccoon photo when raccoons are named; show comments on the real YouTube page by scrolling; cards must exit smoothly and stay centred on screen; fix jerky easing, do not remove; mostly crossfade and dip to black, VHS and flash only rarely; dip to black into and out of every case title card; title card = the project's design.
learnings.text: Owner review 1 of the Farrell sample: real footage first, follow the cut sheet, smooth eased cards that morph, comments on the real page, captions timed to the audio, no stills, show the named animal, mostly crossfade and dip to black, project title card with dips, no channel credit.

learnings.note: Owner review 2 (v2 of the CAMPING-8 3-6 min sample)
learnings.text: Owner review 2 of the CAMPING-8 3-6 min sample (2026-11-09): no ultra-short shots (the 2 s rule was broken); no source cut inside a crossfade (the clip changed mid-fade and looked abrupt); comments as real YouTube screenshots, cropped to the main comment and highlighted, floating up from the bottom or 3D pan, own card only if not found; blur the playing footage behind comments and title cards; nothing still for too long except raw clips from the cut sheet.

learnings.note: Owner review 3 (v3 of the CAMPING-8 3-6 min sample)
learnings.text: Owner review 3 (2026-11-09): no narration shot shorter than 3 s; the comment at 0:24 came and vanished too fast, so remove it (comments need at least 4 s); clips still changed inside crossfades in v3 (soft source cuts the scan missed), so check the final file frame by frame at every fade.

v3 build check (2026-11-09): ffmpeg xfade 'fadeblack' drops the old clip to black in about 7 frames, which looks like a jump; dips now use an even eased custom curve. The location stamp faded during a crossfade; overlays now sit only on the solo part of a shot. Comment rule set to 3.5 s total so the narration timing can hold it.

Research (2026-11-09): subtitle practice (Netflix timed-text guide) keeps each caption 5/6 s to 7 s; reading speed about 15-20 characters per second. Pacing guides say change the picture every 3-7 s and cut B-roll once it has made its point. The Farrell references cut much faster (median shot 0.7-1.3 s), but the owner's rules (narration shots 3 s, mostly crossfades) win. The v4 check found comment motion inside 3 fades and 6 captions under 5/6 s; a rule check script now finds these before render.

Owner on v5 at 0:49: the first comment faded out, the plain footage showed for a moment, then the next comment came suddenly. Then the thread comment faded out, the footage played a moment, and the raw clip crossfaded in: a very short clip. Rule: the motion graphic is part of the video, and its background footage too. Slide the next comment up directly, show the extended thread only (translation already there), and let a comment fade out with its shot's crossfade. rulecheck.py now fails any plain-footage piece under 3 s next to an overlay.

Owner approved all 38 Motion Lab demos: 4 easings (now the Easing palette), 34 moves added to Motion graphics, and the rule changes they need: CRT scan reveal for comments (rule 13), corner OSD/CCTV text with a ticking camcorder clock (rule 5), and one colour-split title per video (Color palette).

Owner rejected Map outline draw and Map crosshair HUD (removed). Timeline strip note: 'a better way to show it' -> redesigned as four real proof cards with dates; the camera moves card to card, the card in focus is sharp, the rest soft and dark. Owner: graphics must look real; film texture belongs on the video, not the graphic.
