graphics_summary: Every built device shows a real artifact: a page, a date, a place, a URL, a comment. Devices enter on a hard cut (0 frames) and ride the shot's own slow linear push (WarpCard is the one exception: warp slide-in). Never: kinetic typography (except VVSentenceFrames for sentences or fate, and one PhraseSlam or ShoutLines per video), burned captions or word pops (except black-box captions on raw clip speech), particles, light leaks, charts or counters (one still big number is fine), tracked graphics (except added text tracked to a word on a captured page), 3D objects, invented infographics. To pick one: find what the narration is doing in the table below, then take the first graphic that fits. Skip "no" items; apply the change an "adapt" item names.

graphics.title: Page plane
graphics.text: Screenshot of the real page on a 3D-angled plane. Edge depth-of-field blur and a vignette. Linear push-in +2.3..+7.3 %/s (typical +5), or tilt down -10..-17 %H/s to read a long page. Wide first, then a macro on the line that matters. Median 8.4 s (2.3-36.7 s).

evidence.label: v01 · Airport website, tilt and scroll down

graphics.use: The narration talks about a web page, article, forum post, channel page or document. Use it for the first view of any captured page.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a video you are about to play (use Video in its page) or for a stock photo.
graphics.why: Shows the real page, so the viewer trusts the claim. The slow push keeps the shot alive and leads the eye to the key line.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Line highlight
graphics.text: Pale yellow box (#DCD896, multiply blend) over the read line. It grows from the line centre outward over 14 frames (power1.inOut), starting 0.25 s before the quoted words. Rides the page plane's push. Variants: G24 Calendar year square: A coloured square sits on one day of a real Wayback calendar page. The page pushes in slowly. The source marks this as low confidence.

evidence.label: v01 · Its a 3d pan zoom with a highlighting effect

graphics.use: The narration reads or names one line, number or word that is visible on the page. Start the box 0.25 s before the words.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the narration does not say the line. Use one box at a time; for a single word on a channel page use Tracked word on a page.
graphics.why: Tells the viewer exactly where to look, so the spoken words and the proof match.
graphics.origin: merged: G24 Calendar year square (review-2026-11-09 MB-98 | C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\STYLE guide\productions\farrell-01-internet-archive\01_reference\MOTION_GRAPHICS_INVENTORY.md)

graphics.title: Video in its page
graphics.text: The watch page on an angled plane with the video playing in its player. Linear push about +5.5 %/s toward the player or the view count. Vignette, soft edges. Variants: ChannelPage (c02_page): Dark channel page, pan to a tile, red box, zoom in, footage plays.

evidence.label: v01 · Tilted YouTube page, view count

graphics.use: You introduce a found video for the first time. Show it in its original platform page, then cut to it full screen. When the video comes from an uploader's channel, start on the channel page, box the tile in red and push in until it plays.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it again once the video is introduced. Play the clip raw and full screen.
graphics.why: Shows where the video came from, so the viewer knows it is real and public.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: Comment card
graphics.text: One comment per shot, over real footage from the case or on the real page it came from (prefer a capture that scrolls to the comment). Parent then reply: the card grows to fit (shape morph) with easing and the reply crossfades in. Eased fade and scale in and out; never pops off. Centred, fully on screen. Median 8.4 s.

evidence.label: v03 · Reddit comment on the shot
v01 · G7 One blog comment isolated: first as a white comment

graphics.use: The cut sheet calls for the comment, or the narration reads what a user said. One comment, then back to the footage.
graphics.avoid: Do not use a comment the narration does not read. Do not retype or invent comments. Do not hard cut inside a thread. Do not run card after card with no footage.
graphics.why: Real comments prove that people saw it. A run of them shows how many reacted and how they felt.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: Year / chapter title
graphics.text: Big gold or red serif word or year over a blurred freeze of the previous shot, or white monospace on a black bar. Fades or rises in, then rides the push. Median 2.7 s (1.6-8.4 s).

evidence.label: v01 · Gold year title '1996' over blur

graphics.use: The narration says a year or date, the story jumps in time, or a new chapter starts. For a chapter break with no date, a VHS chapter turn can carry it.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the date is already on the page on screen. Do not use it for people's names (use Source label / editor note).
graphics.why: Tells the viewer when we are in the story and marks the jump in time.

graphics.title: Mono label over blur
graphics.text: White monospace type on a black box rises in over a blurred copy of the page or thread. Can swap to the English translation in place.
graphics.use: You name the exact thing on screen: a file name, a video title, a username, or the English for foreign text. It can swap to the translation in place.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the text is already readable and in English on the page.
graphics.why: Names the item the viewer is looking at, so they do not have to read the small print. The blur behind keeps the real page as context.

graphics.title: Source label / editor note
graphics.text: Gold #cda75c lowercase humanist sans, bottom-left (left 1.2 %W, bottom 2.1 %H), 3.4 %H tall; editor note fades in 1.2 s ease-out. Source label #d09f61 at 75 % opacity, cuts in at 0 frames.
graphics.use: You credit a source, name a person in news footage, or disclose an edit, for example "music replaced".
graphics.avoid: Do not use it as a caption for words the narration already says.
graphics.why: Shows where the footage came from and what we changed. It builds trust.

graphics.title: UI recreation / typing
graphics.text: A recreated search bar or page (Wayback, YouTube, Google, Translate). Text types letter by letter; a cursor clicks. Dry keyboard or click foley only when the picture shows the action. Median 8.3 s.
graphics.use: The narration says how the person searched for or found something: typing a URL, a search, a click, a translate.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the search step is not part of the story. Cut straight to the result.
graphics.why: Lets the viewer follow the search step by step, so the find feels real.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document

graphics.title: Map / place card
graphics.text: Real Google Maps place card, coordinates panel, satellite or Street View, on a dark background or full frame. Slow push or slide. Median 8.2 s.

evidence.label: v01 · Google Maps place card + Street View

graphics.use: The narration names a real place, a route, a distance, or says how remote somewhere is.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the place does not matter. Never draw route lines or pins that are not on the real map.
graphics.why: Puts the place on a real map, so the viewer feels the distance and the isolation.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place

graphics.title: Split screen / grid / card row
graphics.text: Two clips side by side, photos as vertical panels, or a row of thumbnails or cards. Blurred edges, vignette, slow pan or push. Median 13.2 s.

evidence.label: v01 · Split screen: remote + hotel room

graphics.use: You compare two things side by side, or show all the people or videos at once. Keep to two to four panels or one row.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when only one thing matters. Use Page plane or Photo push instead.
graphics.why: Puts the things next to each other, so the viewer sees the match or the count at one glance.

graphics.title: Glitch / static
graphics.text: Matrix rain, RGB tearing, VHS tracking static, test card or colour bars, as an overlay or a short burst. Median 3.8 s (0.8-7.7 s).

evidence.label: v01 · Wayback home + green matrix overlay

graphics.use: A chapter or tape break with no narration, a video starting up, or screens going dark. About two per 40-minute film.
graphics.avoid: Never use it as a transition between normal shots (use the glitch transition for that).
graphics.why: Breaks the calm and makes the tape feel damaged. It is a pause that adds dread.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny

graphics.title: Photo push
graphics.text: Full-frame photo with a vignette and a slow linear push-in (+2.3..+7.3 %/s). Optional: push in to one face while the others darken and blur. Old photos stay black and white.

evidence.label: v01 · Photo of Brewster at servers, push

graphics.use: The narration names a person or a place and you have a still photo of it.
graphics.avoid: Do not hold a still without a move. If the person needs a name tag, use PhotoNameBar.
graphics.why: Gives the name a face or a place. The slow push stops the still from feeling dead.

graphics.title: Quote card / read-out
graphics.text: The quoted text full screen in white serif over a dark blurred photo, or the post itself tilted. The VO reads it with a filtered voice and the music bed drops out.

evidence.label: v01 · Blog post read-out 'Chicken Pot Pie', tilt
v01 · G25 Read-out: quoted text + filtered voice, bed out

graphics.use: A witness's or the source's own words are read out and the viewer should read them too. The music bed drops out.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the source's own screen shows the text. Show that screen as it is.
graphics.why: Makes the words feel personal and heavy. Silence under the text makes the viewer listen.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message

graphics.title: CurvedArrow
graphics.text: A hand-drawn curved arrow (red, or white on dark footage) draws itself in over a few frames and ends with a head on the named item. It drifts slightly with the shot.
graphics.use: The narration names a video or item on a captured page. A hand-drawn arrow draws onto it as the date fades.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on an item the narration does not name, or on footage that moves. For a single word use Line highlight.
graphics.why: Points to the one item, so the viewer finds it on a busy page.
graphics.fit: adapt: draw it in red (#C6031D) only, on a captured page, riding the page push; no date fade

graphics.title: PhotoNameBar
graphics.text: A portrait with a slow push. A dark red bar sits low with the name in wide-spaced light type and a small corner tick. Two names can show on two boxes.
graphics.use: The narration names a person for the first time and you have a portrait. Use it for an uploader or a victim's companion.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a person with no photo. Use Source label for news footage. For a photo with no name tag, use Photo push.
graphics.why: Ties the name to a face, so the viewer remembers who is who.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the name in VCR OSD Mono, keep the red bar and gold or red accents only, keep the photo black and white, enter on a hard cut

graphics.title: RedWashCut
graphics.text: A hard cut that floods the frame with red and a soft blur. The wash decays fast and the new shot sharpens. A white bloom variant exists.
graphics.use: One time per video, on the scariest line about a place or object. Never on a person.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it twice, and not on a person. For a reveal into a page or photo use FlashBloom.
graphics.why: Marks the single worst moment with a sharp colour hit that fades fast.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny
graphics.fit: adapt: use only the white bloom variant, as FlashBloom; drop the red wash

graphics.title: AliasTile
graphics.text: A small avatar tile, or a "?" tile for an unknown user, with the alias set beside it. The tile flashes for one frame as it cuts in.
graphics.use: The narration names an online alias, a handle or a protected person.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it if the page already shows the avatar. Show the page instead.
graphics.why: Shows there is a name behind the account, but no real face. The one-frame flash makes the name stick.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the alias in VCR OSD Mono; use the real avatar from the captured page when there is one

graphics.title: StockClause
graphics.text: Black-and-white 4:3 stock shots, one per clause. A stamp lands on a shot: a year, a figure (for example $400.000) or red coordinates. The stamp blinks briefly.
graphics.use: Backstory with no footage. Cut one literal black-and-white 4:3 stock shot per clause and stamp a year, a figure or coordinates on it.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when you have real footage or a real page. Never use bright stock.
graphics.why: Fills the backstory with period images and pins it to a date, sum or place.
graphics.fit: adapt: stamp text in VCR OSD Mono; keep the B/W 4:3 grade and a texture layer; one stamp at a time

graphics.title: DeviceInsert
graphics.text: A phone frame sits in the centre third of the frame on a grey radial ground. App captures hold for 12 to 16 s and dissolve in 0.9 to 1.4 s. A rescreen variant shows the screen with sub-pixels.
graphics.use: The narration refers to an app screen, a vertical clip or a webcam still. Show it on its phone or device.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a normal 16:9 clip. For a vertical clip with no device use WindowFrame.
graphics.why: Shows the viewer the exact screen the person saw.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
graphics.fit: adapt: use the dark phone variant on a near-black ground; use a flat frame only; add a slow push

graphics.title: ScreenZoom
graphics.text: A fast push (+154 % in about 5 s) into the screen of a scene, with the screen kept centred. A hard cut then shows the capture full frame. A flash variant ends on a 0.7 s white flash.
graphics.use: "...and on that screen": the shot pushes into a screen in the scene and cuts to the page or clip it shows.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the scene does not show a screen. Do not use a smooth dissolve-zoom.
graphics.why: Links the room to the screen, so the viewer follows from the scene to the evidence.
graphics.fit: adapt: a slow linear push into the screen, then a hard cut or a white flash to the capture; no smooth zoom-through

graphics.title: StockMontage
graphics.text: A run of stock shots, one per noun in a spoken list, each cut on the word time. The grade can switch from normal colour to crime B/W at a chosen shot.
graphics.use: A run of sentences or a spoken list. Cut each stock shot on the time of its noun.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the shots do not match the nouns, or when real footage exists.
graphics.why: Ties each word to a picture, so the list feels fast and concrete.
graphics.fit: adapt: grade every shot dark with a texture layer from the first shot; hard cuts or crossfades only

graphics.title: WindowFrame
graphics.text: The clip sits in a smaller window on near-black instead of filling 16:9. A phone variant shows a 9:16 window on dark grey-green. An optional teal black-and-white grade can be added.
graphics.use: Crime-grade stock, an archive clip or a vertical phone clip that must not fill 16:9. Never blur-fill.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a normal 16:9 clip. If the sides must be filled, use VVBlurFill.
graphics.why: Keeps the clip in its true shape. The dark frame feels like a file or a screen.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
graphics.fit: adapt: add a slow push inside the window and a texture layer

graphics.title: CctvReframe
graphics.text: The CCTV clip is re-framed in steps: punch-ins to a crop, short tints, and in one case a double exposure of a second image over the clip.
graphics.use: The incident clip itself. A key moment is reframed with a punch-in, never slowed.
graphics.avoid: Do not slow the clip. Do not use it on a clip with no key moment.
graphics.why: Moves the eye to the key moment in the raw clip without changing the clip.
graphics.fit: adapt: keep the punch-ins as slow linear pushes and use only grey or red tints

graphics.title: RecOverlay
graphics.text: A light-streak whip, then a huge REC with a blinking red dot on the footage. It can also sit in a corner or as red text.
graphics.use: The narration says "recorded" or "the camera was rolling".
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on footage that is not a camera recording.
graphics.why: Marks the footage as a live recording, so the viewer feels someone was watching.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
graphics.fit: adapt: drop the light-streak whip; cut the REC text in on a hard cut in VCR OSD Mono; keep the small blinking dot

graphics.title: MaskTitle
graphics.text: The platform name as a title, with a drawn mask icon replacing one letter. It pushes in fast at about 3.5 %/s and then cuts.
graphics.use: The narration says the name of the video or platform. A fast push on the title, then a hard cut.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when you have a real capture of the platform page. Use Page plane.
graphics.why: Shows the platform name as a mark, so the viewer links the name to the source.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document
graphics.fit: adapt: set the name in VCR OSD Mono with a red or gold mask accent; end on a hard cut to the next clip, never to a host

graphics.title: PinBoard
graphics.text: Photos and papers pinned or taped on a board, joined by red string. A mugshot can pop on, and a postcard can carry a handwritten place. Grounds are cork, a green mat or a wall. Variants: Evidence board (noc01_evidence_board_v2; v1 nocturne_evidence_board): Photos pinned and joined by thin red lines, slow move.
graphics.use: "Two different cases", "linked both homicides to him", or a suspect or community board.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it with invented items. Use only real photos and pages; keep to two to four items.
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-50 | MT\src\hn\farGrindr\PinBoard.tsx; CATALOGUE.md | merged: Evidence board (noc01_evidence_board_v2; v1 nocturne_evidence_board) (review-2026-11-09 MB-13 | C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\automated-video-workflow\motion-graphics-templates\anim\noc01_evidence_board_v2\ANIM.md; C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\automated-video-workflow\motion-graphics-templates\anim\nocturne_evidence_board\ANIM.md)
graphics.why: Shows how items link in one view, so the viewer sees the connection.
graphics.fit: adapt: use real photos and pages only, labels in VCR OSD Mono, a dark wall ground and red string only

graphics.title: PunchCard
graphics.text: One line of large text, centred on black or on a plate, with one word bold or red. It can build in italic words and dissolves into an image.
graphics.use: The one fateful line, after 0.5 to 2 s of silence. Then it dissolves into the consequence image.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it more than once. It uses the one PhraseSlam / ShoutLines slot of the video.
graphics.why: A hard stop that makes the outcome land.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome
graphics.fit: adapt: count it as the one PhraseSlam of the video; VCR OSD Mono; show the full line at once with one red word

graphics.title: StatusGlyphs
graphics.text: Phone status icons (signal, wifi, battery). One signal bar pings and then goes dark, or a call rings out and stops.
graphics.use: Connection lost, the last ping, a call that rings out. Use it over a real phone screen or recording.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for the narration only "pausing". Do not use it without a real phone screen.
graphics.why: Shows the contact ending, so the silence feels final.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny
graphics.fit: adapt: use it only over a real phone capture, in dim grey with one red element; no pause glyph

graphics.title: FootageNumber
graphics.text: A thin number or short phrase (for example "20 meters deep") inside 4:3 CCTV. In the red variant a red "34" stands over a silhouette while the spot light drops to about 11 %.
graphics.use: A number from the event, written into the real footage. Or a person's age, in red, as the light dies.
graphics.avoid: Do not make it count up. If the number is not in a scene, use FigureCard (one big number).
graphics.why: The number sits inside the real scene, so it lands as a fact.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome
graphics.fit: adapt: keep it still (no count); set the text in VCR OSD Mono; red for an age

graphics.title: NicknameRed
graphics.text: The nickname in big red monospace type, centred over the person's face. The picture is blurred at the edges and sharp in the centre, with a slow push.
graphics.use: The nickname of a killer or suspect, after a beat of silence, over his face.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a victim. Do not use it for a real name (use PhotoNameBar).
graphics.why: Gives the nickname the weight of a label on the face.
graphics.fit: adapt: keep the red monospace text, centred; hard cut in; keep the photo dark with a slow push

graphics.title: WarningSlate
graphics.text: A dark slate with a small warning triangle, or a red warning sign over blurred black-and-white footage. A date can sit on the same slate.
graphics.use: The narration reaches an unsayable act: show a small warning sign. A bare date can use the same slate.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a normal fact. For a content warning before a section use NoticeCard (g-77a5ef76).
graphics.why: Warns without showing or saying it, and keeps the shot clean.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the date text in VCR OSD Mono; keep the warning sign red

graphics.title: CircleCallout
graphics.text: A hand-drawn ring that draws on over a figure in leaked CCTV. A second variant is a black bar over the eyes.
graphics.use: "Look at this figure" in real footage.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on moving footage that needs tracking. For a face use the 404 censor family (g-9312d3b1).
graphics.why: Shows where to look, so the viewer does not miss the figure.
graphics.fit: adapt: draw the ring in red on a frozen frame or a still shot only; it does not track

graphics.title: DataList
graphics.text: A heading and a column of data items on a dark ground, drifting slowly. Variants: blue breach, red alert and green terminal.
graphics.use: The narration lists what was leaked.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the leak is on a real page. Show that page instead.
graphics.why: Shows each kind of data at once, so the viewer feels how much was lost.
graphics.fit: adapt: use the red alert variant only; VCR OSD Mono; slow drift; list real items only

graphics.title: DeniedScreen
graphics.text: A recreated system screen: a big [ACCESS DENIED], a red console, or an admin login panel. The camera is slightly out of focus at the edges.
graphics.use: The system refuses, flags or asks to log in.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a message the source did not show. Do not use it when a real capture exists.
graphics.why: Shows the wall the person hit, in the system's own words.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny
graphics.fit: adapt: recreate only a message the source really showed; red or dark variants only

graphics.title: EmblemWord
graphics.text: The name as a big word with its emblem: a laurel, a flag fill, a neon plate, or placed behind the subject.
graphics.use: An organisation, a concept or a country is named for the first time.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a person. Do not use it for a name already on the page.
graphics.why: Names the group as a mark the viewer can remember.
graphics.fit: adapt: use the behind-the-subject variant, with the word in VCR OSD Mono on a dark plate; drop the neon plate and the flag fill

graphics.title: FringeLines
graphics.text: Lines of article text in an RGB-split sans or a ghost serif, drifting slowly over a plate or over the sea.
graphics.use: The narration reads lines from an article.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the real article can show. Use Page plane with Line highlight.
graphics.why: Gives the lines weight and lets the viewer read as it is spoken.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message
graphics.fit: adapt: set the lines in VCR OSD Mono; one line at a time; drop the Y rotation

graphics.title: NumberToSource
graphics.text: A giant number (for example "50") stands as a dark silhouette. It dissolves into the news page that gave the number.
graphics.use: A number, then the article it came from.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a number with no source page. Use FigureCard.
graphics.why: The number lands first, then the proof follows, so the viewer trusts it.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome
graphics.fit: adapt: keep the number still and in VCR OSD Mono; no count; the page is a Page plane

graphics.title: SilhouetteGroup
graphics.text: Dark silhouette figures stand in a group on a dim ground. One figure is lit (red in the solo variant) and the others dim.
graphics.use: Unnamed people, then focus on one of them. Use it when no photo exists.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when you have a real photo. Use Photo push.
graphics.why: Shows people without faces, so the viewer feels they are unknown.
graphics.fit: adapt: use only black and grey shapes with one red focus; add a slow push and a texture layer

graphics.title: RansomWindow
graphics.text: A recreated lock dialog over an infected desktop, with a headline, paragraphs, payment line and live countdown timers. Screen flicker is optional.
graphics.use: "The message every victim saw" when you have no clean capture.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when a real screenshot exists. Use Page plane.
graphics.why: Shows the message the victim read, in its real form.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document
graphics.fit: adapt: recreate only when no capture exists; freeze the timers (no count); dark variant

graphics.title: SlideDeck
graphics.text: A briefing slide on a dark ground with a classified banner at top and bottom, a logo row, a seal and title, and a flow of labelled boxes and clouds joined by arrows. It rolls slowly.
graphics.use: "The leaked slide": a briefing slide shown as itself.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when you have the real slide image. Use Page plane.
graphics.why: Shows the slide as the source, so the viewer sees a secret document.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document
graphics.fit: adapt: use the real slide as a Page plane; recreate only when no image exists; dark ground with a slow roll

graphics.title: TerminalLog
graphics.text: A console window (Kali style) over a desktop, or full frame. Output arrives in bursts and scrolls. A red margin note labels the step and a red hand-drawn ellipse rings the key line.
graphics.use: A command-line run shown on screen.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when a real capture exists. Use Page plane.
graphics.why: Shows what was run and the result, so the viewer sees the act.
graphics.situation: Show the real page, post or document
graphics.fit: adapt: use a real capture when you can; if you recreate it, use a dark console, one output burst at a time, and a red note and ring in VCR OSD Mono

graphics.title: AccountLadder
graphics.text: A captured account page with a focus box on the profile. It steps to the profile photo, then to the person's name. The locked or tilted page rides a slow push.
graphics.use: The narration introduces a person through their online account. Pick it over Photo name bar (g-63b65632) when the account page is the proof.
graphics.avoid: The person has no account in the story. Use Photo push (g-395610e6) with a name instead.
graphics.why: Shows the real account first, then the face, then the name. The viewer sees how the person was found.
graphics.fit: adapt: use only the real captured account page; set the name in VCR OSD Mono; enter on a hard cut; dark grade and texture on every frame.

graphics.title: ChatBubbles
graphics.text: A chat thread with message bubbles, tilted in 3D or flat. Messages show one after the other with times, on a slow push.
graphics.use: The narration reads a chat between two people. Use it for a thread of messages. For one message, use IMessage (g-ad09e84d).
graphics.avoid: Only one message matters (use IMessage), or the chat is very long (use a Page plane scroll).
graphics.why: Shows the real words in the order they were sent, so the viewer can read along.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message
graphics.fit: adapt: use real messages or a screenshot, not retyped text; dark grade, no bright bubble colours; hard cut in; keep the 3D tilt slow.

graphics.title: CutoutPop
graphics.text: Cut-out pictures of items (a jacket, a shoe) appear one by one over a frosted map or scene background.
graphics.use: The narration lists the objects or clothes of a case (a jacket, a shoe). Use it over a real map or scene; use Split screen / grid (g-3dbd3a0a) when the items are photos of people.
graphics.avoid: The items are not named in the narration, or there are more than four. Use a card row instead.
graphics.why: Puts each item in view at the moment it is named, so the viewer remembers what was found.
graphics.fit: adapt: use real photos of the items; desaturate and add grain; enter on a hard cut with no pop or bounce.

graphics.title: FaceIdProfile
graphics.text: A portrait with rows of pixel-font labels on the left and a red decision box on the right. The chosen face glows and the rest fade. The shot is defocused with RGB noise.
graphics.use: The narration says a system profiled or judged a person, for example a face scan. Use it only when that system is part of the story.
graphics.avoid: The profile output was never shown in the source. Do not invent rows or scores; use Photo push instead.
graphics.why: Shows the person as a machine saw them, which feels cold and watched.
graphics.fit: adapt: use the real labels from the source; set text in VCR OSD Mono; use only red and gold (drop the magenta and cyan variants); keep the heavy defocus and RGB noise low.

graphics.title: IMessage
graphics.text: One text message in a bubble, on a card or inside a phone with contact name and time. It rides a slow tilt and push.
graphics.use: The narration reads one text message. Use it for a single line; for a thread use ChatBubbles (g-54fe306c).
graphics.avoid: The message is not quoted word for word. Use Comment card (g-3cbab747) for a public comment.
graphics.why: Shows the exact message in a phone or card, so the viewer sees it is a real message.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message
graphics.fit: adapt: use a dark-mode or desaturated phone look (not bright blue); show the real message; hard cut in; slow push.

graphics.title: LogoMelt
graphics.text: One logo melts and stutters into a second logo, with a short defocus. The picture then settles on the new logo.
graphics.use: The narration says one company or site was replaced by another (for example one map service became another). Use it once for that fact.
graphics.avoid: The change is not important to the story. Use a hard cut between the two real logos.
graphics.why: The first logo breaks into the second. This makes the change feel like a loss.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome
graphics.fit: adapt: use the two real logos; keep the melt short and dark, like a tape glitch; do not use smear colours.

graphics.title: MaskFill
graphics.text: A person in the shot is filled with a flat white or red shape. The edge is soft and can glow. The shape can dissolve back to the photo.
graphics.use: The narration speaks of an unnamed person, victim or suspect and you must not show the face. Use it instead of a blur when you want a calm, flat shape.
graphics.avoid: The person is already named and shown in a source. Use Photo push; for a face in raw video use Blur patch (g-8718a98d).
graphics.why: Hides the identity but keeps the sense of a person. The viewer feels the gap.
graphics.fit: adapt: keep the white or red fill; use only gold and red accents (drop the two-tone look); the mask must be drawn by hand for each shot.

graphics.title: NamesOnPhoto
graphics.text: A real photo with a name beside each person. The edge is blurred and the photo has a vignette and slow push.
graphics.use: The narration names two or more people who stand in one photo. Use it for a group; use Photo push (g-395610e6) for one person.
graphics.avoid: The names are not said in the narration. Do not put names on faces that the narration did not name.
graphics.why: Puts each name on the right face, so the viewer knows who is who.
graphics.fit: adapt: set names in VCR OSD Mono; use the real photo; slow push; names enter on a hard cut when the narration says them.

graphics.title: PixelLetters
graphics.text: Large letters made of glowing LED pixels sit in the scene. The shot then changes to a sepia satellite view of the place.
graphics.use: The narration names a facility or site and then the story moves to see it from above. Use it for the name and then the swap to the satellite view.
graphics.avoid: The place is not important. Use a Map / place card (g-a6ef4aad) when you only need the location.
graphics.why: Writes the place in the scene, then shows where it is. The viewer links name and place.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place
graphics.fit: adapt: set the letters in VCR OSD Mono; swap to the real satellite image with a crossfade or hard cut; use red or gold light only.

graphics.title: ThresholdDuotone
graphics.text: A photo turned into a two-colour print with hard contrast and film grain. The ink is red or white on black.
graphics.use: The narration names the threat or the object of the crime (a weapon, a tool, a face). Use it on one still image.
graphics.avoid: The image is a source you must show as it is (use Page plane). Do not use it on a photo of a victim.
graphics.why: Turns the picture into a harsh black-and-red print. It makes the object feel like a warning.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny
graphics.fit: adapt: keep ink to black, white or Farrell red only; add a slow push so the shot is not still.

graphics.title: UiCardLift
graphics.text: A user card cut from a captured page, lifted and shown large over a blurred and dimmed copy of the page.
graphics.use: The narration says an anonymous account did something. Pick it over Account ladder (g-0613b90b) when there is no face or name to reach. Same job as Card over its own blur (g-6c457d55).
graphics.avoid: The account has a name and photo. Use Account ladder.
graphics.why: Lifts the real user card out of its page. The viewer sees the account has no name.

graphics.title: ArchiveTreatment
graphics.text: A photo or clip with a black-and-white, news or film grade, grain and slight blur. A place and date line sits below, with a source credit.
graphics.use: The narration uses an archive photo, a newsreel or a news clip. Use it to make clean modern footage look old and real. For a still photo with no extra look, use Photo push.
graphics.avoid: The source is already old or low quality. Do not grade it twice.
graphics.why: Gives the clip an archive look and a place and date line, so the viewer trusts it as a record.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
graphics.fit: adapt: set the place and date line in VCR OSD Mono; credit in the Source label style (g-376107b9); keep old photos black and white.

graphics.title: HudTag
graphics.text: A small bracket label with the name of the object, placed on the shot. It types in and the brackets close around it.
graphics.use: The narration names a thing on screen for the first time (a vehicle, a device). Use it once per object. For a label that follows a freeze, use Freeze label (g-da47e8b4).
graphics.avoid: The name is already on screen or obvious. Do not label every object.
graphics.why: Ties the word to the object. The viewer learns the name when they see the thing.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the label in VCR OSD Mono; use gold or red (drop amber); show it on a hard cut instead of typing it out.

graphics.title: MethodCards
graphics.text: Title cards for each item enter one after the other and stay on screen. The shots behind them change.
graphics.use: The narration says there were several ways, steps or kinds (for example three methods). The cards stay while the shots change under them.
graphics.avoid: The list has more than four items, or the items are not said in the narration. Use Split screen / grid instead.
graphics.why: Gives the list a fixed frame, so the viewer follows each item while the footage moves.
graphics.fit: adapt: plain VCR OSD Mono titles only; no icons or slam motion; hard cut in; dark grade. Use sparingly because it is close to an infographic.

graphics.title: TerminalPanel
graphics.text: A terminal panel with speaker and message lines typed in. A second mode shows a row of numbered badges, one lit at a time.
graphics.use: The narration reads intercepted radio or transcript lines. Pick it for a transcript; for a typed web quote use Typed quote (g-7be66bf5). A row of numbered badges also lists cases 1 to n.
graphics.avoid: The transcript is not real. Do not write lines the source does not have.
graphics.why: Shows the words as a log, so the viewer sees it is a record. The speaker is clear.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message
graphics.fit: adapt: use the real transcript only; set text in VCR OSD Mono; one colour (drop the amber and ice looks); type at speech speed or cut the text in.

graphics.title: ChannelSting
graphics.text: The channel name appears on a dark ground with a soft wipe, holds, and then drops away. Variants show 'presents', 'welcome back' or a typed wordmark.
graphics.use: The video starts with the channel's own ident, before the cold open or right before the title. Use it once.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it between chapters. Chapter breaks use VHS (rule 9).
graphics.why: Marks the start of the video and sets the mood before the story.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the wordmark in VCR OSD Mono; plain hard cut; no outline or bright colour; one use per video.

graphics.title: DisclaimerCard
graphics.text: White text lines on black with a little flicker and bloom. Key phrases show in colour. It holds, then cuts to black.
graphics.use: Frame 0 of the video, before the narration. It shows the viewer-discretion text and then a clean black beat. Use the Farrell preset only.
graphics.avoid: Not mid-video. For a later notice use Notice card (g-77a5ef76); for a list of what is blurred use Notice list (g-5ffaeb0c).
graphics.why: Warns the viewer and sets the tone. The black beat gives the first shot more weight.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the text in VCR OSD Mono (the Farrell preset uses a condensed bold sans); keep the key phrases in red or gold; use the Farrell preset, not the venture or nexpo ones.

graphics.title: NoticeList
graphics.text: A heading and a short list of notices in monospace type, with smeared edges and dropouts, in the cold open.
graphics.use: The cold open warns the viewer in the video's own voice about what they will see or what is blurred. Pick it over Disclaimer card (g-3b4c99d9) only when the list of items matters.
graphics.avoid: The warning is the standard disclaimer. Use Disclaimer card instead.
graphics.why: Tells the viewer what to expect, so the later shocks feel earned.
graphics.fit: adapt: set text in VCR OSD Mono; use white with red keywords; drop the paper and amber variants. It repeats Disclaimer card, so use only one of the two.

graphics.title: RatingSlate
graphics.text: A rating box (TV, MA) with a header, a footer and a list of descriptors, on a plate with a slow push.
graphics.use: The first card of the video, as a broadcast rating box with content descriptors. Pick it over Disclaimer card (g-3b4c99d9) only for a broadcast look.
graphics.avoid: The video is not meant to look like TV. Use Disclaimer card, the Farrell standard.
graphics.why: Says 'viewer discretion' in the language of TV, which sets a dark tone at once.
graphics.fit: adapt: set rating and descriptors in VCR OSD Mono; use white and red only; do not use it together with Disclaimer card.

graphics.title: RedSun
graphics.text: A red sun or moon rises above a dark horizon and shrinks, with a halo and a caption. In the outro it sits over the end credits.
graphics.use: After the warning and before the first case, or as the last image of the video. Use it once.
graphics.avoid: The story is not in analog-horror mode. Use Glitch / static (g-7e744546) for a tape break.
graphics.why: An uneasy image that tells the viewer this is horror. As an outro it leaves a mark.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the caption in VCR OSD Mono; red only; dark grade; keep one use per video.

graphics.title: LEMMiNO Kryptos SectionWall + PhraseLift
graphics.text: Long transcript split into parts; chilling line rises out of the transcript with green glow
graphics.use: A long transcript or log is read and one chilling line is the key. Use it once per video. It counts as your one PhraseSlam / ShoutLines moment.
graphics.avoid: The log is short. Use Quote card (g-aea5881c).
graphics.why: Splits a long text into parts, then lifts the one line the viewer must remember.
graphics.situation: Read a quote, comment or message
graphics.fit: adapt: change the green glow to red or gold; set text in VCR OSD Mono; use the real log; do not add another kinetic line in the same video.

graphics.title: Replay variants (4: SlowReplay, FrameStep, VcrReplay, AdjustedReplay)
graphics.text: Same clip replayed slower, frame by frame, on VCR noise, or colour-adjusted
graphics.use: The narration says 'look again' at a key moment. VcrReplay (STOP, REWIND, PLAY) and FrameStep suit Farrell. AdjustedReplay brightens a dark moment.
graphics.avoid: The moment is clear the first time. Do not replay it. For a held detail use Freeze-push with red circle (g-3c6d677f).
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-135 | MT\src\hn\ hnReplay/SlowReplay, FrameStep, VcrReplay, AdjustedReplay
graphics.why: Gives the viewer a second look at the same frames, with tape marks that fit the mood.
graphics.fit: adapt: use VcrReplay and FrameStep with VCR OSD Mono; use SlowReplay and AdjustedReplay only when the narration asks; keep the audio from the raw clip.

graphics.title: Loupe
graphics.text: A red ring marks an area of the playing clip. A zoomed inset of that area shows beside it, and the rest of the frame dims.
graphics.use: The narration says 'zoom in on the window' or 'the left edge' while the clip keeps playing. Use it for a fixed area. Use Freeze-push with red circle (g-3c6d677f) if the clip can stop.
graphics.avoid: The detail moves around the frame. Use a freeze instead.
graphics.why: Lets the viewer see the detail and the whole scene in one shot.
graphics.fit: adapt: use the fixed ring option, not a tracked ring (tracked graphics are on the Never list); red ring; no extra glow colours.

graphics.title: SpotGlow
graphics.text: The frame turns to mono. The figure keeps its colour and gets a soft glow, held for about 10 s.
graphics.use: The narration says something like 'what appears to be a man can be seen standing by the path'. The figure stays still while the narration doubts it.
graphics.avoid: The figure moves a lot. Use a freeze with a red circle (g-3c6d677f).
graphics.why: Keeps the figure in colour on a grey frame. The viewer looks at it for as long as the narration doubts it.
graphics.fit: adapt: use it only on a figure that stands still, with a fixed glow (no tracking); change the green glow to red or gold.

graphics.title: CallWave
graphics.text: A line or bar wave of the audio runs across the frame, with a caption below. Speakers can have colour cues.
graphics.use: An audio-only case plays (a 911 call, radio, a recording). Use it over a still or dark plate while the raw audio runs.
graphics.avoid: The case has video. Show the video. For a short sound inside a clip use Sound label (g-816af4bb).
graphics.why: Gives the viewer something to watch while they hear the real recording.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
graphics.fit: adapt: draw the wave from the real audio only; speaker words as black-box captions in VCR OSD Mono; one colour for the wave.

graphics.title: EndCredits
graphics.text: Names and short cards scroll up the frame at a steady speed, with small insets beside them.
graphics.use: The end of the video: credits for the sources and the people. Use it only if the video ends on credits.
graphics.avoid: The video ends on the last narration line. Use Source label (g-376107b9) for single credits.
graphics.why: Gives credit where it is due and closes the video with a calm, dark beat.
graphics.fit: adapt: set names in VCR OSD Mono; no heart or icon art; slow scroll on black; credit real sources only.

graphics.title: NoticeCard
graphics.text: One or more lines of text in the middle of the frame, with one accented word. Several pages can follow each other. Variants: Red warning card: Black, red box: 'WARNING / VIEWER DISCRETION IS ADVISED'.
graphics.use: A notice inside the video: a content warning, a skip-time note, an 'epilogue' or a disclaimer. For frame 0 use Disclaimer card (g-3b4c99d9).
graphics.avoid: The text is already on screen. Do not repeat it.
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-146 | MT\src\hn\nexpo\NoticeCard.tsx; CATALOGUE.md | merged: Red warning card (review-2026-11-09 MB-74 | C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\EncountersStudio\refstudy\learnings\MOTIONS.md sec 8)
graphics.why: Tells the viewer what is cut or what is next, in plain text.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the text in VCR OSD Mono; red for the key word only; put it over a dark textured plate.

graphics.title: PhotoNames
graphics.text: One, two or three photos side by side with a name under each, on a dark plate. Variants: Case cards: NocturnCouple + HCE-Couple: Two-person intro plate (couple/pair).
graphics.use: The narration introduces the victims or other people with photos. Pick it over Names on photo (g-bea1704e) when each photo is shown on its own card; pick Photo name bar (g-63b65632) for one person.
graphics.avoid: The people are minors or must stay hidden. Use Eye bar (g-a92fbbff) or MaskFill (g-339e19a6).
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-148 | MT\src\hn\nexpo\PhotoNames.tsx; CATALOGUE.md | merged: Case cards: NocturnCouple + HCE-Couple (review-2026-11-09 MA-225 | PG\hyperframes\compositions\case-cards\NocturnCouple.html, HCE-Couple.html)
graphics.why: Puts a face and a name together at the moment the narration says the name.
graphics.fit: adapt: set names in VCR OSD Mono; old photos stay black and white; slow push on every photo.

graphics.title: DreadWash
graphics.text: A light page tints to saturated red over about 1 s (the detail stays). Thin scan-noise streaks run through it. It ends on a 3-6 frame TV-snow burst, then a hard cut or black.
graphics.use: A normal story turns dark in one sentence. Use it as the exit from a captured page into the dark part. Use it once, not on each page.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on a person. Use a plain dip to black for a date change. Do not use it more than once or twice in a video (see RedWashCut).
graphics.why: The page goes red, then snow, then black, so the viewer feels the story change. It marks the turn without a word.
graphics.situation: Something breaks, goes wrong or feels uncanny
graphics.fit: adapt: keep the red tint and the 3-6 frame TV-snow burst, then hard cut or dip to black; no extra particles or light leak

graphics.title: EyeBar
graphics.text: A solid black bar over the eyes on a full-frame face photo. The bar belongs to the photo and moves with it during a slow push. It is in from frame 0. A black-and-white threshold print version exists.
graphics.use: A victim or a minor is introduced by name and you have a face photo. Put the bar over the eyes while the narration says the name.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on an adult suspect or a public figure. Use MaskFill when you have no photo.
graphics.why: Protects the person, and it still shows that this is a real human. The viewer links the name to the face.

graphics.title: LinkMap
graphics.text: A full-frame page capture gets a red frame and zooms out into the centre card of a node graph. Red lines run to other page cards that enter from outside the frame. Dark red vignette. It holds for about 3 s, then a hard cut. Variants: Link board (noc06_link_board_v3): Thick red rounded frame joining screenshot panels.
graphics.use: The narration says that people online linked the case to other things, or that several sources point to one page. Start on the page and pull back to the other pages around it.
graphics.avoid: Do not invent links or pages. For a fixed board of photos use PinBoard. For accounts that connect use Link board.

oc06_link_board\ANIM.md)
graphics.why: Shows that the claim grew from many real sources, so the viewer sees the web around the case. The pull-back gives a sense of scale.
graphics.fit: adapt: use only real page captures as the cards; thin red lines without a glow; hard cut out

graphics.title: MonoEcho
graphics.text: A dip to black (about 0.5 s out and 0.5 s up). The subject's shot comes up in mono and slowed, with 2 faint trailing ghost copies. A VCR OSD Mono name chip (white on black) sits beside the face. A list form stacks 2-4 chips.
graphics.use: A person is named for the first time, or their sentence and facts are given (for example a prison term). Dip to black, then show the person in mono with the name chip. For facts use a list of chips. Use PhotoNameBar if you have only a portrait photo.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on a clip where the viewer must see colour or detail. Do not use it for a place.
graphics.why: The slow mono shot and the echo make the person feel past and gone. The VCR chips give the name and the facts as plain text.

graphics.title: PaperFrame
graphics.text: The playing shot shrinks inside a light paper border with a thin dark keyline. A handwritten conclusion writes on, either white inside the shot or dark ink on the paper below. The camera drifts slowly. The frame can grow back to full.
graphics.use: The narration draws a conclusion about a shot that is still playing (for example, someone may have been injured here). Use it for one short line. Use ShotNote when the line goes straight on the footage.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the clip should fill the frame. Do not use more than one note per shot.
graphics.why: The paper frame separates the editor's reading from the raw footage. The viewer sees the clip and the claim together.
graphics.fit: adapt: write the note in VCR OSD Mono (typed on, not handwriting); make the paper dark grey, not light

graphics.title: ScrapBoard
graphics.text: Scrapbook board on grey paper, three layouts. Annotate: writing on the shot, then the camera pulls back and an arrow draws to a second still. Pair: two stills with a curved arrow and a line like "Same person?". Grid: a 2x2 grid of bordered stills with labels, then a fifth still.
graphics.use: The narration reasons frame by frame, or recaps the clues so far. Use it to compare two stills ("same person?") or to line up four or five frames.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for one still (use ShotNote or Loupe). Do not use it as a list of invented clues.
graphics.why: Puts the evidence side by side so the viewer can check the reasoning. A slow pull-back keeps it moving.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the labels in VCR OSD Mono; darken the paper; keep the red ellipse and arrows

graphics.title: ShotNote
graphics.text: The shot goes mono, holds, then a white marker conclusion writes on in the lower left at a steep angle, in step with the spoken line. An arrow draws to the subject. A tilt version puts the frame on paper.
graphics.use: The narrator states a conclusion straight on the footage (for example, someone else was inside the school). Use it once per shot, after a hold. Use PaperFrame to put the note on a paper border instead.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the clip is busy or the narration gives no conclusion. Use ArrowLabel for a short silent pointer.
graphics.why: The marker line and the arrow tie the claim to the exact place in the frame. The mono shot makes the footage feel cold.
graphics.fit: adapt: type the line in VCR OSD Mono at a steep angle; keep the white arrow

graphics.title: TitleChips
graphics.text: Two-line title on chips over the playing wall of clips. Line 1 is light grey on a dark chip. Line 2 is red on a black chip. VCR OSD Mono caps. It enters with a 3-4 frame pixel drop-out, holds about 2 s, then cuts out.
graphics.use: The narration speaks the title of the video at the end of the cold open. Put the two chips over the wall of clips.
graphics.avoid: Do not put it on black. Do not use it at a chapter break (use a title card).
graphics.why: Names the video at the moment the viewer is hooked, over real clips, in the channel's own font.
graphics.fit: adapt: enter on a hard cut; keep the pixel drop-out only as a 3-4 frame glitch

graphics.title: ArrowLabel
graphics.text: A thick red arrow with a bold caps label (for example VICTIMS SLEEPING), or thin red leader lines with lower-case *asterisk* labels. Everything pops in on one frame and holds across cuts. Silent. Variants: EdgePointer: A solid red block arrow (about 300 px) points down-left at the subject. It pops in on one frame and can carry a short label.
graphics.use: The viewer must see one thing in a frozen or paused shot, and the narration does not say where. Use the arrow with a short caps label, or the leader line with an asterisk label. For a subject at the edge of the frame or just out of shot, use one solid red block arrow that points at it.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the narration already points to the detail. Use CircleCallout for a round mark.
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-190 | MT\src\hn\nocText\ArrowLabel.tsx; CATALOGUE.md | merged: EdgePointer (review-2026-11-09 MA-136 | MT\src\hn\hnReplay\EdgePointer.tsx; CATALOGUE.md)
graphics.why: Shows where to look without a word. The red mark is easy to read on a dark frame.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the labels in VCR OSD Mono instead of Arial bold; keep the red; pop in on one frame

graphics.title: CensorSound
graphics.text: The clip is blurred (sigma about 40 px) with a dark vignette. A black chip sits at the centre with a red censored word such as (g*ns**ts). A second form shows the clip in a 4:3 inset window on near-black. Hard cut in and out.
graphics.use: A sound is too violent to play or show, such as gunshots or screams. Put the censored word over a heavily blurred clip.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a sound the viewer needs to hear (use SoundLabel). Do not use it to hide a picture (use EyeBar or the 404 censor family).
graphics.why: The viewer knows what the sound was without hearing the worst of it. The asterisks make the censoring part of the look.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the word in VCR OSD Mono, red on the black chip, not Times italic

graphics.title: SoundLabel
graphics.text: A sound cue in VCR OSD Mono on a tight black box at bottom centre, for example *Josh hears footsteps*. It holds about 4.5 s and cuts in and out with the shot.
graphics.use: A sound in the raw clip matters and the viewer might miss it, such as footsteps. Show the label while the sound plays.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for sounds that are loud or obvious. Use CensorSound if the sound is unshowable.
graphics.why: Tells the viewer what to listen for, so a weak sound carries weight. It is a plain, quiet cue.

graphics.title: VVBlurFill
graphics.text: The vertical clip plays full height in the middle. The same clip, enlarged, blurred and scan-lined, fills the sides, with a dark falloff at the clip edges. A credit tag such as YT: NAME and a small caption sit on top. A print mode shows a landscape photo as a white-bordered print over its blur.
graphics.use: A vertical TikTok, Shorts or phone clip must play on a 16:9 timeline, for 2-5 s, with its creator credit. Use it for each vertical clip.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on 16:9 footage. Use WindowFrame for crime-grade stock, or DeviceInsert if you must show the phone itself.
graphics.why: Keeps the phone clip whole and shows where it came from. The blurred fill avoids black bars.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
graphics.fit: adapt: set the credit tag and the caption in VCR OSD Mono; keep the scanlines on the fill and darken the blur

graphics.title: VVRetroWindow
graphics.text: A retro desktop window springs open on black, titled "visual venture". The portrait grows inside it. The person's name types on in a mono face with a blinking caret and a faint colour fringe. 3-4 s. Variants: VVRetroWindowGX: The upgrade of VVRetroWindow. It has a glossy bevel, a red and cyan colour edge on the left, top and bottom edges bowed like a CRT, and a horizontal glitch streak that flashes across the frame while the window opens.
graphics.use: A person is named for the first time (within about 30 s of a chapter card). Show the portrait in the window while the name types on. The GX variant adds a short glitch streak as the window opens.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for every person. Use PhotoNameBar or NamesOnPhoto when you have only a photo.
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-200 | MT\src\hn\vv\VVRetroWindow.tsx; CATALOGUE.md | merged: VVRetroWindowGX (review-2026-11-09 MA-207 | MT\src\hn\vvMore\VVRetroWindowGX.tsx; CATALOGUE.md)
graphics.why: The retro window makes a person feel like a file on an old computer. The typed name gives the viewer the name and the face together.
graphics.fit: adapt: remove the brand name "visual venture" from the title bar; type the name in VCR OSD Mono; open the window on a hard cut

graphics.title: LocationStamp (overlay)
graphics.text: A place name stamp over footage. The place is large, in capital letters. A smaller mono line sits under it (for example the date or coordinates). Variants: LocationStamp: Top-left stamp: place, date, detail. VCR location title: Centred near bottom: place big, sub-line small.
graphics.use: The narration names where the footage was shot. Put the place name on the footage as the narration says it. For a place with no footage use a Map / place card.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the place does not matter. Do not use it on a map shot (the map already names the place).
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-216 | PG\hyperframes\compositions\overlays\location-stamp.html | merged: LocationStamp (review-2026-11-09 MB-61 | C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\EncountersStudio\refstudy\learnings\MOTIONS.md sec 1); VCR location title (review-2026-11-09 MB-72 | C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\EncountersStudio\refstudy\learnings\MOTIONS.md sec 8)
graphics.why: Anchors the clip to a real place. The viewer knows where they are before the action starts.
graphics.situation: Name a place or move to a new place
graphics.fit: adapt: set both the place and the meta line in VCR OSD Mono; no extra glow

graphics.title: Glitch number (Glitch2025)
graphics.text: RGB-split glitch where the last digit flips from one value to the next
graphics.use: The date or day changes on screen (2025 to 2026, DAY 1 to DAY 2). Flip the last digit once.
graphics.avoid: Do not count up through many values. Use Year / chapter title for a big jump, and a dip to black for a new period.
graphics.why: The glitch tells the viewer that time moved, in a way that feels like a damaged tape. Use it for a short jump, not a new chapter.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the digits in VCR OSD Mono; flip once; no count-up

graphics.title: KW frame-circle
graphics.text: Still of a figure with an animated ring drawn round it Variants: LEMMiNO Kennedy PhotoMarkup + LineupStage: Pointers/boxes on an archival photo; silhouette police line-up. Radar rings (noc02_radar_rings): Red rings pulse out over a dark photo.
graphics.use: The narration says "look at this figure" or "look at this detail" over a still. Draw a ring round it as the narration says it. For a moving clip use CircleCallout.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the detail is already large. Do not leave the still without a push.
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-221 | PG\hyperframes\compositions\kw\frame-circle.html; hyperframes\notes\kw.md | merged: LEMMiNO Kennedy PhotoMarkup + LineupStage (review-2026-11-09 MA-127 | MT\src\hn\ lemKennedy/PhotoMarkup, LineupStage); Radar rings (noc02_radar_rings) (review-2026-11-09 MB-34 | C:\Users\ayush\Videos\CLAUDE\automated-video-workflow\motion-graphics-templates\anim\noc02_radar_rings\ANIM.md)
graphics.why: The ring tells the viewer exactly where to look. It makes a small detail the point of the shot.
graphics.fit: adapt: use a red ring only; push the still slowly while the ring draws

graphics.title: Case cards: NocturnChannelPlate + HCE-ChannelPlate
graphics.text: Channel/uploader plate with avatar and name
graphics.use: The narration introduces the channel or uploader of a found video. Use the plate when you do not have the real channel page. When you have the page, show it with Page plane.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the real channel page is available (use Page plane). Do not use it for a person who is not an uploader.
graphics.why: Names the source of the footage and gives the uploader a face. The viewer sees who posted it.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the channel name in VCR OSD Mono; use the real avatar; hard cut in

graphics.title: camping8: channel-plate, channel-v3, dossier, theories, side-by-side, ir-replay
graphics.text: Six hyperframes files: channel-plate, channel-v3, dossier (Courier and Geo text), theories (Bebas and VCR), side-by-side (two clips) and ir-replay (an infrared replay with a rewind mark).
graphics.use: A set of files from the camping8 build: channel plate, case dossier, theories list, two clips side by side, and an infrared replay. Pick by job: dossier for a case file, side-by-side to compare two clips.
graphics.avoid: Do not use the two channel plates or the theories list as new designs. For a compare use Split screen. For a channel intro use Page plane.
graphics.why: Each file does one job for a camping case: who posted it, what the file says, what people think, and a compare view.
graphics.fit: adapt: keep dossier and side-by-side only; set all text in VCR OSD Mono (dossier uses Courier and Geo; side-by-side and theories use Bebas)

graphics.title: 404 library: footage family (10)
graphics.text: Ten templates in the 404 library: DashHold, CrtTv, PhonePanel, Replay, PipCam, Letterbox, AngleSync, RadioWave, FloatingClipCard. Each frames a clip in a TV, a phone, a small window or a replay. Variants: CrtBox: The clip plays inside a rounded CRT screen with barrel bend, grille lines, RGB split and vignette. It can be full size or an inset, and it has a slow push.
graphics.use: A clip needs a frame that shows where it came from: a TV or CRT, a phone, a picture-in-picture, or a replay. Pick the frame that matches the real source.
graphics.avoid: Do not use a frame that does not match the source. Use the Replay variants for "look again". Do not use a bright or playful frame.
graphics.origin: review-2026-11-09 MA-238 | MT\INDEX.md; MT\src\templates\footage\ | merged: CrtBox (review-2026-11-09 MA-62 | MT\src\hn\farIsrael\CrtBox.tsx; CATALOGUE.md)
graphics.why: The frame tells the viewer what kind of footage this is, so the clip feels real.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)

graphics.title: 404 library: evidence family (11)
graphics.text: Eleven templates in the 404 library, including Corkboard, DeskSpread, StackFlyThrough, TiltedWall, SplitCompare, CitationSheet and CardWall. They show several documents or photos on a board, a desk, a wall or a stack.
graphics.use: The narration lists several documents or photos in a case. Use a spread or a wall of real items. Use SplitCompare for two items.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for one item (use Page plane). Do not fill it with invented items. Use PinBoard for items that link.
graphics.why: Shows the volume of evidence at once, so the viewer feels the case is real and large.
graphics.fit: adapt: use real captured items only; slow linear push; no fly-through or spin; dark ground

graphics.title: 404 library: censor family (5)
graphics.text: Five templates in the 404 library: TrackedBlur, Mosaic, CutAway, CensorCard and PosterCard. They hide gore or a face. Variants: CensorMarks: Two forms. TrackedMosaic: hard-edged mosaic blocks (about 65 px) over a region of the footage. RedactedDoc: a light article page under a dark vignette with a slow push, solid black bars over names, and a red marker bar that wipes behind the key phrase.

graphics.avoid: Do not blur what the narration needs to show. For a face in a photo use EyeBar; for a sound use CensorSound.

graphics.fit: adapt: use a fixed or keyframed region for the blur or mosaic (no tracked graphic); set CensorCard and PosterCard text in VCR OSD Mono

graphics.title: Upgrade targets, other (StepRamp, MeasureOnSat, MeasureOnPhoto, FloatingClipCard
graphics.text: Four templates. StepRamp: a stepped freeze ramp (slow build-up, then 2-3 exact-frame holds). MeasureOnSat and MeasureOnPhoto: a dashed red bracket with a typed value on a satellite image or photo. FloatingClipCard: a small clip card floating over its own blur.
graphics.use: The narration gives a size or a distance (use the bracket on a satellite image or photo), or a fast event needs exact freezes (use StepRamp), or a found clip is introduced (use FloatingClipCard).
graphics.avoid: Do not use the bracket on an invented map. Do not slow an incident clip without a reason. FloatingClipCard repeats the footage family.
graphics.why: The bracket turns a number into something the viewer can see on a real image. The stepped freeze makes a fast event readable.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome
graphics.fit: adapt: set the bracket value in VCR OSD Mono; hard cut the bracket in; use a real satellite image or photo; no typed count

graphics.title: Excerpt heading (noc11_ex1_heading_v3)
graphics.text: Big white/red words pulled from a page, rest faded

graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the full page must show (use Line highlight). Do not retype the heading in a new look.
graphics.why: Pulls the one line that matters out of a long page. It is faster to read than the full page.
graphics.fit: adapt: fade the rest of the page to dark; keep the page's own font; use white or red words only

graphics.title: Analysis board card + pan (noc01_board_card_v3, noc01_board_pan, nocturne_analys
graphics.text: A pale board sheet. Cards scale in one by one. The camera pans across the board. (Files: noc01_board_card_v3, noc01_board_pan, nocturne_analysis_board.)
graphics.use: The narration walks through a theory or an analysis, point by point. Show one card per point and pan across the board.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for one point. Use ScrapBoard for frame-by-frame reasoning on stills.
graphics.why: The pan follows the narration from one point to the next, so a long theory stays clear.

graphics.title: CCTV wall zoom (noc01_cctv_wall_zoom; v1 nocturne_cctv_wall_zoom)
graphics.text: Many camera feeds as a wall, zoom to one
graphics.use: The narration talks about surveillance or many cameras. Show the wall of feeds, then zoom to the one that matters.
graphics.avoid: Do not fill the wall with invented feeds. Use CctvReframe when you only need the one incident clip.

graphics.title: Numbered case grid (noc10_case_grid, noc10_case_grid2_v3)
graphics.text: Six panels with red numbers 1-6
graphics.use: A list video starts, and the narration previews the cases that follow. Show six panels with numbers 1 to 6.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the video has few cases. Do not animate the numbers as a count.
graphics.why: Tells the viewer what is coming and how many cases there are.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the numbers in VCR OSD Mono; panels are real clip stills; slow push

graphics.title: Inset clip (noc13_inset)
graphics.text: Video inset with white frame border over footage
graphics.use: The narration points to a second clip that matters while the first clip plays, for example a reply video or a second angle. If the two clips must have equal weight, use Split screen (g-3dbd3a0a).
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for a clip that needs full attention. Play it full screen instead.
graphics.why: Lets the viewer see both clips at once without a cut.
graphics.fit: adapt: enter on a hard cut, keep the frame border dim (not bright white), add a slow push, and grade the inset to match the main shot

graphics.title: Freeze label (noc07_freeze_label)
graphics.text: A raw frame freezes. A thin white box draws round one spot and a short label names it in a pixel font. The label sits next to the box.
graphics.use: The narration names one small detail in raw footage. Freeze the frame, box the spot and name it. If you only need to mark the spot, use Freeze-push with red circle (g-3c6d677f).
graphics.avoid: Do not use it when the detail is clear in the live clip. Do not stack it with a second callout.
graphics.why: Stops the picture so the viewer finds the detail and learns its name.
graphics.fit: adapt: set the label in VCR OSD Mono, enter on a hard cut, and add a slow push on the frozen frame (no still graphics)

graphics.title: Outcome chip / stack (noc08_outcome_chip, noc08_outcome_stack_v3)
graphics.text: One or more dark chips hold lines of pixel text, for example 'Lifetime Ban On Possessing Firearms'. The stack version shows several lines together.
graphics.use: The narration states what happened to one person at the end of a case, for example a ban or a sentence. For several people in a row, use VVSentenceFrames (g-7ef6980a).
graphics.avoid: Do not use it for facts that are not an outcome. Do not use it as a caption.
graphics.why: A hard line of text makes the outcome land.
graphics.situation: Stress a number, fact or outcome
graphics.fit: adapt: set the text in VCR OSD Mono, enter on a hard cut, no typing or bounce, and show one chip at a time over a dark, moving shot

graphics.title: PLAY OSD (noc08_play_osd_v2)
graphics.text: VCR 'PLAY >' on-screen display, 0.33 s
graphics.use: A found video is about to play. Show 'PLAY >' for a short moment, then play the clip. Use this when the video is a tape or file; use Video in its page (g-3ebc1993) when it comes from a web page.
graphics.avoid: Do not use it on every clip. Do not use it on a clip that was never a tape or recording.
graphics.why: Makes the viewer feel they press play on a real tape.
graphics.situation: Show a video in its context (platform, CCTV, phone, file)
